neighbours.label: a word, or its first split piece, that plays something down as tiny or trivial (minuscule, trifle, trite, banal, seemingly anything)
fire: His share of the profits was tiny and almost negligible beside theirs.
Neighbors there will argue over the most petty of things.
She got a paltry sum for all those years of service.
Compared to the whole budget, this cost is minuscule.
The film's ending felt banal after such a clever opening.
He gave up his career for a mere trifle of an offer.
The speech was full of trite slogans and tired jokes.
These mundane details hardly matter in the larger story.
quiet: His share of the profits was generous and well above theirs.
Neighbors there will gather for the best of meals.
She got a large pension for all those years of service.
Compared to the whole budget, this cost is enormous.
The film's ending felt moving after such a clever opening.
He gave up his career for a major offer from abroad.
The speech was full of bold promises and fresh ideas.
These crucial details really matter in the larger story.

notes: Card: ' tr' x4, ' min' x3, ' no' x3, ' seemingly' x2, ' ban' x2, ' is' x2: minuscule, trifle, trite, banal and Spanish minúsculo. The shared pattern is 'this is small or unimportant', and it fires on the first piece, before the word is finished. Probes: seemingly 0.757, trite 0.749, minuscule 0.716, trifle 0.431; 'large' 0.042, 'fight over the old farm' 0.247. New cases are in the test (negligible, petty, paltry, mundane).
